messages:
Luis (Support): FYI customer ACME reported a sudden increase in tail latency and auth 401s earlier today, and their bill spiked. They say requests that should hit eu-west are going to us-west. Attaching excerpts.
Devon (Routing): can you paste the request headers + the routing decision ID? we need to trace which policy matched.
Luis (Support): request example: `POST /v1/generate` header `X-Region: eu` auth ok. Decision id `dec-2026-03-17-1422`. log shows decision -> region=us-west, fallback_reason=`policy_order_mismatch`
Luis (Support): Quick log snippet:
```
2026-03-17T14:21:03Z dec-2026-03-17-1422 matched_policy_id=pl-998 evaluated_preferences=[{"priority":1},{"priority":2},{"priority":3}] selected_region=us-west
```
Devon (Routing): weird, evaluated_preferences show correct numeric priorities but selected_region is wrong. Can someone grab the policy JSON stored for pl-998?
Maria (Platform): fetched policy from DB (redacted ids):
```
{
  "id":"pl-998",
  "rules":[
    {"region":"eu-west","priority":1},
    {"region":"us-west","priority":2},
    {"region":"ap-south","priority":3}
  ],
  "ui_meta":{"rank":[3,2,1]}  // legacy field from console v1
}
```
Erin (SRE): ah — there is a `rank` array leftover from the old console migration. runtime merge code currently prefers the last-seen ordering and treats `rank` as authoritative when present. That would invert expected priority for some code paths.
Devon (Routing): confirm: runtime merge logic:
```
final_order = ui_meta.rank || rules.map(r => r.priority)
```
so if `rank` exists it overrides `rules`. For pl-998 `rank` is [3,2,1] which flips the order.
Luis (Support): that would explain requests being routed to us-west (rank[0]==3 -> region with priority==3 -> us-west). Customer was on eu-first traffic, so auth tokens were validated against eu region and failed when they hit us.
Erin (SRE): also seeing auth token validation errors in the same window: `token_issuer_mismatch` when token audience included `eu.project`. SRE logs show 1200 hits routed to us-west in 15m.
Devon (Routing): how did `rank` end up in DB? migration script that copied UI ordering into `ui_meta.rank` for console v1 users. it was supposed to be removed but we left it as a fallback. new console writes `rules` only.
Maria (Platform): reproducer locally: insert a policy with `rules` + `ui_meta.rank=[3,2,1]` then run `./bin/routing-sim --policy pl-998 --seed 42` -> picks us-west. attaching command output.
routebot: routing-sim run complete: chosen_region=us-west; expected_region=eu-west; reason=ui_meta.rank precedence
Devon (Routing): mitigation: hotfix the runtime merge to prefer explicit `rules` ordering over legacy `ui_meta.rank`, and add a migration job to remove `ui_meta.rank` from active policies.
Erin (SRE): agree. also throttle rate and roll out fix to canary subset (10% of traffic) to ensure no regression. add an ephemeral fallback to honor token issuer check before finalizing region selection so we can short-circuit mismatches.
Luis (Support): I'll reply to ACME explaining root cause (legacy rank field) and ETA for mitigation. They are asking for immediate rollback option — can we flip a feature-flag to force `rules` precedence?
Devon (Routing): yes. `FEATURE_FORCE_RULE_ORDER=true` can be toggled via infra service. I'll flip on canary now and monitor.
Erin (SRE): flipped on canary 10% at 14:45 UTC. preliminary telemetry: cross-region hits down 80% in canary cohort, auth 401s down. rolling to 100% in 15m if no regressions.
Maria (Platform): scheduling a cleanup migration: `DELETE FROM policies WHERE ui_meta.rank IS NOT NULL RETURNING id` then apply `UPDATE` to reconcile ambiguous ones. need approval for bulk write window.
Devon (Routing): add unit test for merge precedence and e2e test where `ui_meta.rank` conflicts with `rules`. Also add an alert if `ui_meta.rank` != null shows up in any new writes.
Luis (Support): thanks team. ACME notified. marking incident as escalated -> awaiting postmortem. :thumbsup:
